title: Working at Redwood — Onboarding, Roles & Career Ladders, Benefits and Internal Tools (2026)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview
------
This page consolidates Redwood's employee-facing handbook sections relevant to working at Redwood: culture and expectations, role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks, hiring and onboarding flow, and a concise internal tools guide. It is intended as a single reference for new hires and managers.

1) Working at Redwood — culture & expectations
------------------------------------------------
Short intro: Redwood is an engineering-centric, product-led company focused on building a production-first inference platform. We expect direct communication, ownership of outcomes, and a bias toward measurable progress. New hires should expect:

- Clear goals and measurable objectives for the first 90 days.
- Regular 1:1s with managers and a peer onboarding buddy for the first 3 months.
- Documentation-first decision making; write before you build where possible.
- Inclusive collaboration across product, infra, and research teams.

Key behavioral expectations:
- Ship with quality: prioritize reliability and observability for any production change.
- Communicate early: raise blockers in standups and PR descriptions.
- Be data-informed: use observability/metrics to inform design and tradeoffs.

2) Roles & career ladders (engineering & product examples)
------------------------------------------------------------
This section summarizes role bands and typical expectations. Managers should use the detailed career-ladder rubric (linked in related pages) during calibration and promotion cycles.

Engineer ladder summary (example):

| Level | Title (typical) | Key expectations | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| IC1 | New Grad / Associate Engineer | Deliver defined tasks, learn codebase, request feedback | Component-level |
| IC2 | Software Engineer | Own stories end-to-end, reliable implementation, unit tests | Service-level |
| IC3 | Senior Software Engineer | Design subsystems, mentor others, drive medium projects | Cross-service |
| IC4 | Staff Engineer | Technical leadership, system design, cross-team influence | Platform/Org |
| IC5 | Principal Engineer | Company-level architecture, technical strategy, long-term vision | Company-wide |

Product ladder summary (example):

| Level | Title | Key expectations |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Associate PM | Drive small features; partner closely with engineering |
| P2 | PM | Define roadmaps for features, own metrics and tradeoffs |
| P3 | Senior PM | Cross-product initiatives, stakeholder management |
| P4 | Lead PM / Group PM | Product strategy for major product areas |

Promotion & calibration notes:
- Promotions are evidence-based: impact, scope, craft, and leadership.
- Candidates should submit a promotion packet (summary, examples, manager letter).
- Quarterly calibration meetings include people-ops, managers, and cross-functional reps.

3) Benefits & perks (high level)
----------------------------------
Summary: Redwood offers a competitive benefits package designed for high-performing teams and distributed employees across North America and Europe. Highlights below; detailed plan documents live with People Ops.

Health & wellness:
- Medical, dental, and vision plans with multiple tiers (US plans + comparable EU options).
- Flexible health stipend for contractors and non-standard locations.
- Mental health support: EAP and counseling credits.

Financial & equity:
- Competitive base salary bands with hire/band transparency guidance.
- Annual equity grants for full-time employees (grant cadence varies by hire date and level).
- 401(k) plan with company matching (US) / pension guidance (EU).

Time off & family:
- Flexible paid time off (manager-guided), 12 company holidays (region-adjusted).
- Parental leave: 16 weeks primary caregiver paid leave + 6 weeks secondary caregiver (region policies apply).
- Volunteer & wellness days (2 days/year).

Work setup & stipends:
- Home office stipend at hire and annual refresh budget.
- Commuter and travel reimbursement for in-person team events.
- Hardware policy: company-supported laptops and accessories.

Learning & development:
- Conference budget, training stipend, and internal learning days.
- Mentorship program and internal tech talks.

Perks & community:
- Quarterly company offsites, monthly team socials, interest-based Guilds.
- Referral bonus program.

4) Hiring process & onboarding overview
----------------------------------------
High-level hiring flow (Engineering example):
1. Recruiter screen (role fit & logistics)
2. Technical screen (coding or take-home, depending on role)
3. Onsite / virtual loop (systems design, product sense, execution, culture add)
4. Manager loop & peer interviews
5. Offer & compensation discussion
6. Background check & formal acceptance

Expected timelines:
- Typical time-to-offer: 2-4 weeks for standard roles, varies for senior ICs.
- People Ops will provide an offer pack within 72 hours of verbal approval.

Onboarding checklist (first 90 days) — manager responsibilities and new hire tasks:
- Pre-boarding (before day 1): create accounts (Okta, GitHub, Slack), order hardware, assign buddy, share first-week agenda.
- Day 1: HR orientation, benefits enrollment guidance, short product overview, team intro.
- Week 1: Setup dev environment, read core docs (architecture overview, coding standards), small starter task.
- Month 1: Deliver first scoped change, attend architecture/product overviews, set 30-day goals.
- Month 2: Take ownership of a component, conduct cross-team walkthroughs, set 60-day goals.
- Month 3: Drive a customer-impacting change, complete onboarding feedback survey, set 90-day objectives and performance check-in.

Sample 30/60/90 goals (new engineer):
- 30d: Development environment configured; complete 1 bugfix or small feature; meet cross-functional stakeholders.
- 60d: Deliver a medium-sized story; own one service's minor release process; mentor a peer on a task.
- 90d: Lead design for a component improvement; demonstrate measurable latency/cost improvement on a small experiment; complete onboarding checklist.

New hire manager checklist (quick):
- Assign buddy and 1:1 cadence, review first 30/60/90 plan, ensure access to observability dashboards, set clear success signals.

5) Internal tools guide (concise)
----------------------------------
Purpose: list primary internal tools, owners, and quick access / first steps for new hires. People Ops and platform teams maintain access flows.

- Okta (SSO & access management) — Owner: Security. First steps: enroll MFA, complete identity verification. Contact: identity@redwood.ai
- Slack (team communication) — Owner: Eng-DevX. Join #all, #announcements, team channels. Add profile and working hours.
- Confluence (internal docs) — Owner: People Ops / Eng-DevX. Bookmark company-handbook and your team space.
- GitHub (code & PRs) — Owner: Eng-DevX. Request repo access via the onboarding ticket; follow branching & PR templates.
- Redwood Console (internal tools for infra & cost dashboards) — Owner: Eng-Platform. Request console role access during pre-boarding; onboarding includes a guided tour.
- CI/CD (build & release pipelines — e.g., GitHub Actions / internal runners) — Owner: Eng-Infra. Read release runbooks before shipping.
- Jira (tickets & roadmaps) — Owner: Product Ops. Join your team board; use issue templates for bugs and stories.
- VPN / Bastion (private deployments & secure access) — Owner: Security. Apply for access via IT ticket; complete training where required.

Access & security reminders:
- Principle of least privilege: request only the access you need to perform your role.
- All access requests should be made through the standard IT onboarding ticket. Exceptions require manager approval.
- Sensitive work (customer data, private deployments) requires additional confidentiality training and NDA acknowledgements.

6) Manager & People Ops responsibilities
-------------------------------------------
Manager responsibilities during onboarding:
- Set clear priorities and measurable goals for the first 90 days.
- Check 1:1s weekly (first month) then bi-weekly.
- Review and provide timely feedback on early PRs and design docs.

People Ops responsibilities:
- Coordinate pre-boarding, benefits enrollment, and company-level orientation.
- Maintain and update this page yearly or on policy changes.
- Operate the mentorship and inclusion programs and manage learning budgets.

Feedback and updates
---------------------
If you have suggestions for clarifications or discover outdated links, open an edit request or contact people-ops@redwood.ai. This document undergoes a formal review every 6 months and ad-hoc updates when policies change.
